_comment: Phase 5, AC-4. The Japanese-to-Indonesian glossary as DATA: llm.py quotes these lines into the prompt verbatim for lang='id' and check_id asserts the output against them. docs/honorifics.md is the prose statement of the same policy; check_id asserts the two agree. Edit both.
policy: Write natural, idiomatic Indonesian as a published manga translation would: short spoken sentences, no English scaffolding, no word-by-word gloss.
Register follows the speaker: casual dialogue uses aku/kau/kamu and dropped particles; formal or deferential speech uses saya/Anda; narration boxes use standard written Indonesian.
Japanese honorific suffixes are KEPT in romaji, attached to the name with a hyphen, exactly as the table below renders them; never translate -san as Bapak/Ibu and never drop a suffix the source has.
先輩 and 先生 as forms of address are rendered per the table, and the same way every time they occur for the same speaker.
Brand names, abbreviations and Latin-script tokens in the source stay as they are; sound effects are rendered as Indonesian onomatopoeia, not left in kana.
Do not add translator notes, explanations, or brackets.

honorifics.use: neutral politeness; kept as a suffix on the name
affectionate, children and close friends; kept
senior at school or work; as address or suffix, always senpai, never Kak
teacher, doctor, artist; as address or suffix, always sensei, never Pak/Bu Guru
a name with no suffix stays bare: intimacy or contempt, and the reader must see which
